title: Is the Ramsey number of the prescribed cycle against any graph at most twice the latter's edge count plus the allowed correction?
scope: For every cycle length k>=3, there is an edge threshold M(k) such that every finite simple graph H with no isolated vertices and at least M(k) edges satisfies R(C_k,H)<=2|E(H)|+floor((k-1)/2). The threshold is uniform over H for fixed k; the theorem includes triangle, quadrilateral, larger even and larger odd cycles. R is the usual two-colour, ordinary non-induced graph Ramsey number. No bound for every small edge count, optimal explicit threshold, induced-copy variant, or exact Ramsey-number formula is claimed.
attribution: Existing formalization by Codex / GPT-5.6 Sol. The 2026 general-cycle theorem is by Stijn Cambie, Andrea Freschi, Patryk Morawski, Kalina Petrova and Alexey Pokrovskiy ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10238v1)). The fixed source also retains earlier credits to Paul Erdos, Ralph Faudree, Cecil Rousseau, Richard Schelp, Wayne Goddard, Daniel Kleitman, Alexander Sidorenko and C. J. Jayawardene. Original source bytes and attribution notices are preserved; the two inaccurate given names in its header are clarified below. No new-proof or first-formalization claim.

source_history_notes: Selected source bytes are unchanged from plby/lean-proofs commit 8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e, with Lean/Mathlib 4.33.0 advertised by the source headers.

The Ramsey foundations encode arbitrary finite simple graphs on Fin n, prove isomorphism invariance, and define the least two-colour ordinary-copy Ramsey threshold using a proved existence theorem. No fixed-vertex-count restriction is added to the original problem.
The statement is eventual in |E(H)| with a threshold depending on the cycle length k but not on H. Graphs with isolated vertices are outside the stated hypotheses.

All 75 custom modules were compiled from unchanged source bytes. The checker actually replayed the Erdos570 target and 72 dot-separated descendant modules; the two other custom foundation modules were compiled and imported, and Mathlib was reused from the pinned cache.

The 2026 general-cycle result is by Stijn Cambie, Andrea Freschi, Patryk Morawski, Kalina Petrova and Alexey Pokrovskiy ([primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10238v1)). The immutable source header spells two given names as Alberto and Piotr and abbreviates Kalina; these header bytes are preserved for source fidelity, but mathematical attribution here follows the primary paper. Earlier special-case credits and the source's Codex / GPT-5.6 Sol formalization credit are retained.
